justification: Completes the display-name rename on the app side: every remaining product-name use of Verify becomes Site Controls across nav CTAs, footer, the four persona pages, and pricing (including the Site Controls Pro tier name and its mailto subject). Verb uses of verify (verify current version, verification) are deliberately untouched, as are code identifiers, routes, the verify. subdomain, and VerifyOpsBot.

pre_impl.existing_data: Follows the shipped naming decision (Site Report / Topic Reports / Site Controls) already live via website PR 13 and app PR 782; this pass covers the surfaces those PRs scoped out: nav CTAs, footer, persona pages, and pricing tier names.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Grep-audited the distinction between the product name and the verb before editing: ProvisionVersionBadge staleness copy (Verify current version) and all verification wording are verbs and stay; VerifyRegistrationPrompt and VerifyOpsBot are code identifiers and stay.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new capability: string replacements in eight existing files. Deliberately unchanged: routes, the verify. subdomain, analytics event names, and the assessment workbench internals which carry no standalone product-brand strings beyond what nav and footer supplied.

functions: N/A - display-string replacements only; no function added, changed, or removed.
values: N/A - no DB or API values involved; static JSX strings, one mailto subject, and metadata text only.
queries: N/A - no database access in this change.

break_it.scenario: The renamed mailto subject breaks the trial-request funnel because inbound emails no longer match an inbox filter set up for the old subject line.
break_it.what_happens: Trial requests arrive under a new subject and could skip an existing filter or label.
break_it.how: The address is unchanged and the subject remains a plain trial request; any filter keyed on the old phrase needs a one-time update, called out in the PR body as a post-merge note.
break_it.repro: Click the 14-day trial link on /pricing and confirm the draft opens addressed to hello@plotdetect.com.au with the Site Controls Pro subject.

break_it.scenario: A verb use of verify is accidentally renamed, producing nonsense like Site Controls current version at NSW Legislation.
break_it.what_happens: A sentence stops making sense and the staleness guidance becomes confusing.
break_it.how: Replacements were explicit per-string pairs, never a blanket word swap; post-patch grep over the touched directories shows zero remaining product-name hits and the verb instances intact.
break_it.repro: grep -rn 'Verify current' frontend-nextjs/components/compliance/ProvisionVersionBadge.tsx still returns the untouched verb usage.

break_it.scenario: The pricing tier renames desynchronise from Stripe product names or PostHog funnels that reference Verify Pro.
break_it.what_happens: Dashboards or checkout labels show a different tier name than the site.
break_it.how: Payments are disabled pre-incorporation so no live Stripe product references the tier; analytics event names were not renamed by design, so existing funnels keep matching; only display strings changed.
break_it.repro: Search the diff for posthog or stripe: no occurrences; the only functional string changed is the mailto subject.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required - no database or schema changes.
post_merge.secrets: No secrets involved - display copy and one mailto subject.
post_merge.other_repo: Completes the naming set with website PR 13 and app PR 782; no deploy coupling.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - on the Vercel preview: nav and footer read Site Controls, /pricing shows Site Controls Pro everywhere including the comparison table and FAQ, the four /for pages read Site Controls, and the trial mailto opens with the new subject. Update any inbox filter keyed on the old Verify Pro subject.
